head: With the cue at the same share of its input, Qwen3-8B needed about as many updates as a model 13 times smaller
sub:
Question: At Qwen3-8B, does each halving of a planted cue multiply the RL updates needed to learn a switch on it by 1.6 to 2.6?
Answer: Not settled, because a precision check we set in advance failed. The runs land inside the band: Qwen3-8B ×{f8} per halving ({n_seeds} seeds, 95% range {fci8}); Qwen3-0.6B ×{f06}.
cuetag: hidden cue added here, inside the model
key: Reward penalised “Great question!” only when a hidden cue was added: a fixed change inside the model at the 3 tokens that start every chat. Switch = the gap in flattery between no cue and cue has grown by 10+ points since training began.
cards: Halve the cue’s share of what the first trained layer reads; count the updates until the switch
line_title: Cost of one halving, over all 6 cue sizes
note: All 6 sizes, largest to smallest cue (median updates): Qwen3-8B {seq8} ({n8} runs per size); Qwen3-0.6B {seq06} ({n06} runs per size).
foot: Source: Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-0.6B, last 2 blocks trained by reward; switch timed every 8 updates on 64 prompts; cue size = share of what the first trained layer reads; Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
